# Best RV power station and solar combo

For an RV, check three things: a 30A/RV outlet, enough AC output for your air conditioner (a 13,500 BTU unit draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup [6]), and a solar input that can take the panels you plan to buy.

## My picks

**Best value for a big RV system: ALLPOWERS R4000 plus about 2,000 W of panels**
- It has 3,456 Wh of LiFePO4, 3,600 W continuous at 120 V, a dedicated RV outlet, and a 5-year warranty [1].
- It accepts up to 2,000 W of solar across three inputs, at 650 W each. You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W [1].
- The price is $1,499, or $1,319.12 with code EXTRA12. The code needs an order over $1,200 and expires 2026-11-15. The store's checkout has the final word [1].
- Caveats: it weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it isn't hand-carry portable. Sale items can't be returned, and the buyer pays return shipping unless the unit is defective [1].
- [Buy the ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, and the seller earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Best for full-time boondocking and running the AC: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous, and 8,000 W surge. It expands past 12 kWh and recharges 0–80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet [6].
- It's heavy enough that moving it is a two-person job, and it's the priciest option once you add expansion batteries [6].
- I don't have its solar input spec or a current price. The older DELTA Pro accepted 1,600 W of solar [3].
- Details: [RV power station comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**Best mid-range with a 30A RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, up to 1,200 W of solar input, and weighs about 62 lb [6][7].
- It suits multi-day trips with a fridge, Starlink, and light loads. Its surge is rated at 3,600 W, so a roof AC is a stretch [6].
- Details: [Camping power station roundup](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Best for weekend trips without an AC: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 plus two SolarSaga 200W panels**
- It has 1,070 Wh and 1,500 W output, weighs about 23.8 lb, and has a 400 W solar cap. Two 200 W panels use all of that [7].
- It isn't expandable [7].
- Details: [same roundup](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

## Choosing solar panels
- Size the array to the station's solar input limit, because extra panels beyond it won't charge any faster [7]. Check the voltage range as well.
- One source says a 300–400 W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun [6].
- For smaller setups, [4] suggests a Renogy 200W foldable solar suitcase. The sources don't give panel specs or prices.

## What I couldn't verify
Apart from the ALLPOWERS link, the sources gave me article pages rather than direct retailer product links. The prices they list for the other models are inconsistent and some may be outdated, so confirm current price and specs on the seller's page before buying.

If you tell me your RV's AC size and how many days you boondock, I can narrow this to one pick.
